content:
This PR is blocking some improvements to mathlib's multigoal linter. I have reviewed it, and it looks good to me (and mostly like a very straightforward metaprogramming refactoring).
@François G. Dorais @Kim Morrison @Wrenna Robson Can I nominate this for merging?

@Michael Rothgang agreed that it is both sensible and useful. I would like to improve the tests a little bit - arguably they were already deficient - but to be clear that is insurance as much as anything. If that happens to my satisfaction I'd be happy to approve this.

Thanks for the quick look! The comment about tests is very reasonable. @Jovan Gerbscheid Do you have a moment to look into that? (I am excited about your multigoal linter PR; it would be great to see if this rewrite is possible.)

I've left a comment on GitHub. Essentially, while I think this PR is a step in the right direction, what I would really like is some more generic goal-management API (see GitHub for more details about this suggestion).
While obviously Lean is not Rocq, I do think there's something to be said for looking what our cousin does and consciously choosing what syntax to use or not.
I'm not really an advocate of that in general but when it comes to tactics and goal management this is I think reasonably well-trodden ground
I'm mostly out of commission due to a shoulder injury. I'll defer to Wrenna and Kim.
I think batteries#1990 is good to be merged. Feel free to ping me when the mathlib adaptation PR is ready.

Thanks! @Jovan Gerbscheid When you have had a moment to update #44446 (to include a batteries bump), feel free to ping me and I'll merge. If you don't have time to do this, I'm also happy to take over.
@Michael Rothgang, it can be merged in its current state already, and then the batteries bump can go after that.

As @François G. Dorais pointed out, another set of adaptations is necessary. I have locally fixed the tactic linter side (which had no mathlib tests): #44484 adds such tests. I'll push my other changes in a moment.
#44485 is a manual dependency bump, which passes these tests.
CC @Jovan Gerbscheid this might resolve your ping here. (In any case, feel free to take a look!)
